claims.text: An active-learning-trained MLIP trained on diverse ab initio solid and liquid configurations can bridge the reference–target phase-space gap encountered with traditional EAM references in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method applies to both solid and liquid phases near or above alloy melting temperatures.
Nb–Mo–Ta is an example alloy within the proposed scope.
High-entropy carbonitrides are an example material class within the proposed scope.
The EAM reference in TOR-TILD should be replaced by an MLIP trained using active learning on ab initio solid and liquid configurations.
Active learning can produce a potential that accurately describes both liquid and solid phases of high-entropy carbonitrides.
The applicable alloys have nearly equiatomic compositions containing four to eight principal elements.
The applicable temperature range is above 2000 K or near the experimental melting temperature.
The MLIP captures a diverse range of local atomic environments, including chemically disordered and thermally displaced configurations.
The MLIP accurately represents many-body interactions that traditional EAM does not describe well.
Capturing more local environments enhances phase-space sampling.
The trained MLIP reproduces ab initio forces and energies across solid and liquid configurations.
Accurate reproduction of ab initio energies and forces across solid and liquid configurations improves reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved reference–target overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD using EAM references.
The intervention may reduce thermodynamic-integration errors by a quantity on the order of tens of meV per atom compared with EAM references.
Traditional EAM references have limited configurational representation in the liquid state.
The benefit of the MLIP intervention may diminish for lower-melting systems or systems already described well by simpler potentials.

The proposed comparison can falsify the hypothesis if the MLIP does not produce a statistically significant reduction in path mismatch or improvement in phase-space overlap relative to the EAM control.

contradictions.description: Nb–Mo–Ta is given as an example within scope, but it contains only three principal metallic elements whereas the stated applicability range requires four to eight principal elements.

The intervention defines the comparison as replacing an EAM reference with an MLIP reference, while the experiment describes paths from a harmonic reference to the full ab initio system without clearly specifying how EAM and MLIP serve as the respective integration references.
